chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, from al-Maqani'i, from Bakkar ibn Ahmad, from Hasan ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Bakir, from Abdul Malik ibn Ismail al-Asadi, from his father who said: Narrated to me Saeed ibn Jubair
He said: 'The year in which the Mahdi will rise, it will rain twenty-four times; its effects and bounties will be seen.'

key_terms.الْمَهْدِيُّ: The Guided One, referring to Imam Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (a.s)
key_terms.يَقُومُ: He rises/stands (referring to the rise/Qiyam of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of rain associated with the year of Imam Mahdi's reappearance?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration from the chain of Ibn Bakir highlights a specific meteorological sign of the end times, where twenty-four distinct rains in the year of the Mahdi’s rise signify divine favor and agricultural abundance. This phenomenon is interpreted by Shia scholars as a tangible manifestation of the earth’s release from its constraints, serving as a visible blessing (barakah) that confirms the legitimacy of his global justice.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 435 - It is narrated from Ahmad bin Ali Raazi from Maqani from Bukkar bin Ahmad from Hasan bin Husain from Abdullah bin Bukair from Abdul Malik bin Ismail Asadi from his father that he said: Narrated to me Saeed bin Jubair that:
“It will rain twenty-four times in the year in which Imam Mahdi (a.s) will reappear; and its effects and bounties would be clear.”
